task.description: Step 0.5 + Step 1 for ISS-0444: registry lookup, then root-cause diagnosis of Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1's broken 'never raises' contract for a tenant schema whose Postgres schema is missing entirely. Diagnosis only -- ISSUE-FIXER does not implement the fix (WF-03 Step 1 explicitly reserves fix design for CODE-DESIGNER); route accordingly.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 -- REGISTRY LOOKUP: grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for 'undefined_table|undefined_schema|tenant_schema_missing|schema_missing|dropped.*schema'. Ten resolved/open hits (ISS-0050, ISS-0110, ISS-0048, ISS-0109, ISS-0115, ISS-0114, ISS-0116, ISS-0260, ISS-0292, ISS-0416) -- all are TEST-SUITE flakiness where a tenant schema is dropped mid-test by TenantSchemaReaper/sandbox cleanup racing a live test, a different mechanism (test-harness race, not a production code path with a missing rescue). None match ISS-0444's shape (a production GenServer with an undocumented raise on a genuinely-absent schema). No prior resolved entry for this exact defect; this is a fresh diagnosis, not a recurrence.

STEP 1 -- DIAGNOSIS, confirmed by direct reproduction (not from the issue's prose alone). Ran, against the real test Postgres instance (MIX_ENV=test mix run -e, Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(:auto)):
  Letflow.Scheduler.claim_due_timer_ids("nonexistent_schema_xyz_999", 10)
Actual output:
  raised struct: Postgrex.Error
  message: "ERROR 42P01 (undefined_table) relation \"nonexistent_schema_xyz_999.timers\" does not exist ..."
  pg code: :undefined_table
So Postgres reports the whole-schema-missing case as 42P01/:undefined_table on the fully-qualified relation (not a distinct :undefined_schema code) -- confirms the issue text's 'undefined_table/undefined_schema' framing is one single observed error shape, not two to handle differently.

ROOT CAUSE: lib/letflow/scheduler.ex claim_due_timer_ids/2 (line ~199-211) builds an Ecto query and calls Repo.all(query, prefix: tenant_schema) with zero try/rescue. poll_and_fire/1 (line ~166) calls claim_due_timer_ids/2 as its very first statement, also with no try/rescue, so the raise propagates straight out of poll_and_fire/1 -- directly contradicting that function's own @doc: 'Never raises -- every per-timer failure is caught internally and folded into the returned counts (design Sec2.2, Sec2.5)'. The per-timer isolation this doc refers to (fire_timer/2's own Repo.transaction/rescue, confirmed by reading lines ~230+) only covers failures AFTER claim succeeds; the claim step itself has no such boundary.

BLAST RADIUS, confirmed by reading lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex handle_info(:tick, _) (line ~101-124) in full: schemas is Enum.each'd, and each schema's poll_and_fire call is wrapped only in with_admission/3 (line ~135), whose own try/after only guarantees the admission unit is released -- it has NO rescue, by design (its own comment: 'fun is responsible for its OWN existing rescue boundary, if any; this wrapper adds admission accounting only'). poller.ex's moduledoc explicitly states (lines ~28-32) that no redundant try/rescue is placed around the Enum.each specifically BECAUSE poll_and_fire/1's own contract is trusted to already guarantee no-raise. Since that contract does not actually hold, an unrescued raise inside with_admission's fun.() propagates out of Enum.each, out of handle_info/2, and crashes the Letflow.Scheduler.Poller GenServer entirely for that tick -- every OTHER tenant schema's timer poll that tick is also lost (Enum.each aborts on the first raised element), not just the schema with the missing physical schema. The supervisor will restart Poller (assuming a normal one_for_one/permanent child spec -- not independently re-verified in this diagnosis pass, flagged for CODE-DESIGNER to confirm the restart doesn't itself retry against the same bad schema in a tight crash loop if that schema sorts early in tenant_schemas()'s query ordering), but every tick lost this way is timers not firing platform-wide, not just for the one bad tenant -- MAJOR-leaning impact despite the issue's filed MINOR severity; flag severity for CODE-DESIGNER/REVIEWER to reconsider given the platform-wide (not per-tenant) blast radius confirmed here.

WHY EXISTING TESTS DID NOT CATCH THIS: grepped test/letflow/scheduler*/ -- all existing Scheduler/Poller tests operate against schemas the test setup itself provisions (sandboxed, physically present); none exercise a tenant_schema string that is syntactically valid (passes TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's regex) but physically absent from Postgres. This exact gap (Registration row present / migrations_applied_at set, but physical CREATE SCHEMA either never completed or was dropped out-of-band) was never constructed in any fixture.

FIX BOUNDARY DECISION (task explicitly leaves this to ISSUE-FIXER's judgment; diagnosed but NOT implemented, per WF-03 Step 1's own 'does NOT implement the fix' rule): recommend the fix belongs INSIDE Letflow.Scheduler (wrapping claim_due_timer_ids/2's query, or poll_and_fire/1's call to it) rather than as a poller.ex call-site rescue matching the maybe_run_* pattern. Reasoning: poller.ex's moduledoc already documents a real architectural distinction between the two catching styles it uses -- the four maybe_run_* sweeps (alert_detection, ordering_cycle, ordering_sweeper, ordering_metrics) wrap their OWN call site in try/rescue _ -> :ok precisely BECAUSE the callees (Letflow.Obs.Alerts, Letflow.Ordering) carry no never-raises contract of their own; poll_and_fire, by contrast, is architecturally supposed to carry that contract AT SOURCE (its own @doc says so, and poller.ex's moduledoc explicitly declines to add a redundant call-site rescue for exactly this reason). Patching only at the poller.ex call site would leave poll_and_fire/1's own documented contract still false when called directly (e.g. from a test, or any future caller that isn't Poller) -- a purely-cosmetic fix that papers over the symptom at exactly one call site instead of making the cited contract true at its source. This is a genuine design decision, not mechanical, because it also determines: (a) what poll_result() shape a caught missing-schema error should produce for THIS tenant_schema (the current type has no error/skipped variant -- claimed/fired/errored/exhausted all describe timer-level outcomes, not a whole-schema-unavailable outcome; CODE-DESIGNER needs to decide whether to add a field, return a sentinel, or document that claimed/fired/errored/exhausted all stay 0 for a skipped schema), and (b) the Logger.warning/1 call's exact skip-and-continue wording/metadata, matching the precedent already established this cycle by REQ-218 at lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex:37-49 (Logger.warning with an ISS-#### tag prefix and structured context) and lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:588-593 (component:/ref: keyword metadata) -- CODE-DESIGNER should pick one of these two established shapes rather than inventing a third.

SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME DEFECT CLASS, found while checking the other 5 poller.ex operations per the task's step 3: maybe_run_retention_sweep/2 (poller.ex line ~152) calls Scheduler.run_retention_sweep(schema_name) inside with_admission with NO try/rescue of its own -- same gap shape as poll_and_fire. Traced run_retention_sweep/1 (scheduler.ex line ~564) into EventStore.archive/1 (event_store.ex line ~1006): archive/1 first calls TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix), confirmed by reading tenant_provisioning.ex:195-208 to be PURE STRING PARSING (regex + UUID.cast on the schema-name text) with zero DB access -- it does NOT verify the physical schema exists, so it succeeds even for a dropped schema and does not shield what follows. archive/1 then proceeds to compute_archive_target_event_ids(prefix, retention_days), which queries the events table with that prefix -- not independently reproduced against a genuinely-missing schema in this diagnosis pass (time-boxed to the two calls the issue names), but by the same Ecto/Postgrex mechanism confirmed above this is assessed HIGH-confidence, not certain, to raise the identical Postgrex.Error :undefined_table shape, unrescued, with the identical Enum.each-crashes-the-tick blast radius. The other 4 operations (alert_detection, ordering_cycle, ordering_sweeper, ordering_metrics) are NOT affected -- each already wraps its own call in try/rescue _ -> :ok inside its with_admission closure (confirmed by reading all four in poller.ex). Recommend CODE-DESIGNER treat this as IN SCOPE for the same fix run: it is the same defect class (missing-schema raise with no rescue, inside a Scheduler-contract function reached via with_admission), reachable via the same tenant_schemas() list, and only enabled conditionally (retention_enabled?/0 + retention_due?/1) -- meaning it is currently masked in most deployments/tests (retention defaults to disabled per @default_retention_enabled false) but is a live landmine the moment REQ-188's retention feature is turned on for a tenant whose schema later gets dropped. Recommend fixing scheduler.ex's run_retention_sweep/1 (or EventStore.archive/1 itself) in the same design pass rather than filing a second issue for a defect already fully diagnosed here -- but this is CODE-DESIGNER's/REVIEWER's call on scope, not asserted as mandatory; if CODE-DESIGNER scopes it out, recommend filing a fresh ISS-#### immediately (per core-directives.md's 'No Issue Left Local-Only') rather than letting it go untracked.

SECURITY-REVIEWER: recommend NOT required. This is an internal background-sweep resilience fix (add error isolation to an already-internal, non-API-exposed polling loop) -- no new API surface, no change to what tenant data is read/written/returned, no auth/tenant-isolation boundary touched (the fix only decides what happens when a boundary that already exists, at the Postgres schema level, is crossed by an operational anomaly). Confirmed against security-invariants.md's INV-1..INV-8 headings (tenant isolation, auth, secrets, audit) -- none apply to 'catch a raise and log a warning inside an already-per-schema-scoped loop.' REVIEWER (OTP idiom, scope creep, decision-record consistency) is the correct and sufficient hard gate here.

NOT IMPLEMENTED: per WF-03 Step 1 and this agent's own role definition, no code or test changes were made in this step. lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex, and test/ are unmodified -- `git status --porcelain` shows only this handoff file added.
result.recommendation_to_orch: Route to Step 2 CODE-DESIGNER: design the fix boundary INSIDE Letflow.Scheduler (recommended: wrap claim_due_timer_ids/2's Repo.all call, or poll_and_fire/1's call to it, in a rescue that converts a Postgrex.Error/undefined_table into a defined, documented outcome) so poll_and_fire/1's own '@doc Never raises' claim becomes literally true at its source, matching poller.ex's own moduledoc's stated assumption rather than patching only the poller.ex call site. Design must specify: (1) the exact rescue clause and match pattern (Postgrex.Error with postgres.code in [:undefined_table, :undefined_schema] specifically, not a bare `rescue _ ->`, to avoid masking unrelated bugs inside the same query), (2) what poll_result() reports for a skipped schema (new field vs. all-zero counts vs. a distinct return shape -- current @type has no slot for 'schema unavailable'), (3) the Logger.warning/1 message and metadata, following either the backfill.ex:37-49 or alerts.ex:588-593 precedent, (4) whether to fix lib/letflow/scheduler.ex run_retention_sweep/1 (or EventStore.archive/1) for the identical latent defect found in maybe_run_retention_sweep/2 in this same pass, or explicitly scope it out with a new filed issue, (5) whether poller.ex's moduledoc's 'no redundant try/rescue around the Enum.each' reasoning (lines ~28-32) needs a documentation update once poll_and_fire/1's contract is fixed at source (likely: leave as-is, since the fix restores rather than changes that architecture -- but CODE-DESIGNER should confirm explicitly rather than silently leave stale). TEST-DESIGNER (Step 4) must construct a tenant_schema string that passes TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's format check but has NO physical CREATE SCHEMA backing it (distinct from a schema missing only one table), confirm the tick completes for OTHER schemas in the same run without the Poller GenServer crashing, and follow the fail-then-pass + mutation-testing discipline WF-03 requires. No SECURITY-REVIEWER needed (confirmed above); REVIEWER is the sufficient gate after ELIXIR-DEV implements.
